name: バインセオ サイゴン 新宿店 (Banh Xeo Saigon Shinjuku)

claims.text: The menu includes a dedicated 'Mon Chay' (vegetarian/vegan) marked section distinct from the standard dishes.
Weekday lunch includes an all-you-can-eat salad bar of roughly 15 kinds of fresh, domestically sourced vegetables.

FindMeGlutenFree listing: Benitsuru is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease; contact the establishment directly to inquire about safety precautions. No celiac-grade positive reviews present.
Waffles (ワッフル) are offered as a separate walk-in item; sources describe them without confirming rice flour, leaving wheat waffles as a plausible cross-contact source in the same small kitchen.

Allergen guidance: rice-flour products in Japan frequently contain blended wheat, Japan has no cross-contamination labeling obligation, and such products are often processed in rooms that also handle wheat — so 'made with rice flour' does not equal celiac-safe.

Signature dishes are built on bacon, fried egg, hollandaise sauce, marmalade and honey (e.g. 'Bacon and Fried Egg' ¥2,200 with honey, marmalade, bacon and hollandaise), with no vegan alternative — confirming vegan = no.

The pancake batter itself is made with rice flour and kibi (raw cane) sugar rather than wheat flour and granulated sugar — described by the owner as a deliberate choice to make a lighter pancake that's easier to digest.

The lunch service pairs gluten-free/vegan mains with a self-serve salad buffet that also includes homemade (wheat) bread and soup in the same buffet area, a potential cross-contact point for celiac-level guests.

Celiac review reports the restaurant refuses to serve celiacs because they make everything with the same equipment, and gluten-free options were in the same case as the normal cakes so the cross-contamination risk was extremely high; the establishment is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease.

Japan has no strict gluten-free standard and no mandatory cross-contamination labeling; rice-flour products can be processed on the same line as wheat, so celiacs must confirm cross-contact directly rather than rely on a GF menu label.

BiOcafe's menu includes animal-derived dishes (eel, egg, chicken) alongside vegan items, and no public source specifies whether katsuo/bonito or other animal dashi is used, so vegan status of individual dishes is unconfirmed.
Vegetables used across the menu are 100% pesticide-free and grown without chemical fertilizer, sourced from farmers chosen for sharing the cafe's health-focused standards.

The gluten-free veggie burger replaces the wheat bun with one made from rice flour and konjac flour and uses only plant-based sauces and "veggie meat," making it fully suitable for a vegan diner avoiding wheat.
Runs a standing monthly-changing healthy lunch explicitly marketed as gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan.

name: ビストロ デ マニラ (Bistro de Manila)

claims.text: No information found on dedicated gluten-free preparation, allergen labeling, or cross-contamination controls; kitchen is small (19-seat restaurant) and shared for all dishes.
Signature adobo dish is braised in a soy-sauce-and-vinegar sauce; standard Japanese/Filipino soy sauce contains wheat and no wheat-free (tamari) alternative was mentioned.

name: 欧風カレー ボンディ 神保町本店 (Bondy (Jimbocho Main Store))

claims.text: All curries share one wheat-flour-and-butter brown-sauce base (roux simmered with meat stock, wine, fruit and vegetables) — there is no separate gluten-free sauce or preparation area.
The curry's richness comes from generous butter and dairy plus beef/pork stock cooked into the single shared sauce base; no vegan menu or dairy/meat-free substitution was found.

name: Cafe de Forte (カフェ・ド・フォルテ)

claims.text: Venue's own site: 「全てのメニューがグルテンフリーではありません」(not all menu items are gluten-free) — wheat dishes share the kitchen, so cross-contact is a real risk for celiacs.
JP celiac guide: 「メニューに小麦成分が含まれているかどうかは、お店で確認してください」(check with the shop whether an item contains wheat).
米粉メニューだけでなく小麦粉を使った通常メニューも提供 — the cafe offers regular menus using wheat flour alongside rice-flour menus, so wheat flour is actively handled in the same kitchen (cross-contamination risk).
アレルギー完全対応ではございませんので、ご注意ください — the shop explicitly states it does NOT provide complete allergy accommodation.
メニューに小麦成分が含まれているかどうかは、お店で確認してください — independent JP GF guide warns wheat may be present and to confirm with the shop rather than assume safety.
米粉パンなどの米粉製品には、グルテンなど小麦を含む原材料が使用されていることがあり、アレルギー事故も発生しております — Japanese Consumer Affairs Agency notice: rice-flour products can contain wheat/gluten and allergy accidents have occurred.

Unverifiable 'dedicated gluten free / I am celiac and felt safe' claim cited address 2-chōme-10-19 Kasuga, which does not match the official 2-14-9 小石川Jフラッツ; the FindMeGlutenFree page could not be fetched (403). Treated as unreliable/conflated, given no weight.
Savory items such as the 醤油麹 (soy-sauce koji) yakitori bowl use soy sauce, which contains wheat unless tamari; confirm before ordering.
Kitchen uses dairy (yogurt, butter, ice cream), eggs and meat throughout; no dedicated vegan prep noted.
The cafe caters to gluten-intolerant/celiac guests and asks allergy guests to notify staff in advance 「アレルギーをお持ちの方は事前にスタッフにお知らせください」, but states 「アレルギー完全対応ではありません」(not fully allergy-compliant).
Core menu is built on domestic rice flour (国産米粉100%) — GF pancakes, waffles, bread, roll cake and Morioka rice-flour cold noodle.
Acai bowl uses additive-free, gluten-free rice-flour granola (米粉の無添加・グルテンフリーのグラノーラ).
Owner-cook explicitly welcomes celiac and gluten-intolerant guests and cooks health-first, additive-free food.

name: カールヴァーン トウキョウ (CARVAAN TOKYO)

claims.text: CARVAAN TOKYO is certified as a Muslim-friendly shop by the Islamic Center of Japan; the kitchen uses naturally derived, halal-certified ingredients imported from around the world and states dishes contain no chemical seasonings, alcohol, or pork-derived ingredients.
Specific menu items are explicitly labeled vegan and halal, including the falafel, hummus and tahini-based dips, and a vegan version of the chicken curry.
Restaurant listing guidance indicates food allergies and disliked ingredients should be communicated in advance, and requests made on the day of the visit may not be accommodatable.

CHOMPOO offers a dedicated multi-course vegan tasting menu (6 to 8 dishes) made only from seasonal vegetables, fruits, beans and herbs with no animal products — including appetizers, a Kao Yam herb salad, soup, a warm main, and plant-based dessert with tea.
The restaurant is additive-free and MSG-free across its menu.
